notes: Auto-executed tool call on hermes: the recipe asks hermes to run `echo hello` with its `terminal` tool and reply `done`. Hermes prompts only for DANGEROUS commands (approvals.mode 'smart'), and `echo hello` classifies as neither hardline nor dangerous (verified against tools/approval.py), so the call auto-executes with no approval window and the canonical arc is ready→working→ready with state NEVER entering waiting. Hermes persists no transcript file: the whole trace lives in one shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db, observed via agent.ProcessOwnedStore. The tool call is visible there as an assistant row with finish_reason='tool_calls' carrying function.name='terminal', closed by a `tool` row with the matching tool_call_id (parser.go maps these to assistant_message+ToolUses and tool_result); the turn settles working→ready when the newest assistant row carries finish_reason='stop' → turn_done, which is an EXPLICIT boundary rather than an idle heuristic (watcher.go turnIsDone). The phase DSL has no tool-event form, so the auto-executed call is asserted via the single uninterrupted working span plus the no-waiting invariant, and verified out-of-band in state.db at record time. Hermes carries a Process matcher, so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real `sessions` row is INSERTed only on the first user message — session_birth is therefore anchored to start UNPINNED so the presession cannot steal identity and cascade failures, turn_start establishes the real session, and turn_done chains off it via same_session_as. Same shape as the sibling opencode ProcessOwnedStore cell. `model` is deliberately NOT pinned: the recording home's config.yaml is provisioned at record time, so record fills it from the recording.

text: The hermes session appears in ready. Unpinned: the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s after it), not at launch, and a transient proc-<PID> presession may appear first.
The tool-requiring prompt drives the hermes session ready → working; message_count grows while the newest row is not assistant/finish_reason='stop', so the activity event is non-terminal.

The `terminal` call auto-executes inside the working span (assistant/tool_calls → tool row closing by tool_call_id) and the turn completes → back to ready on the SAME session once the newest assistant row carries finish_reason='stop'; state never entered waiting.
